short: Speech-task ECoG cursor control (M04) and 1-mm microgrid control (M05) are standard: closed-loop speech-cortex and word-task ECoG BCIs preceded it; imagined vowel pairs were never tested.
position: The paper [@leuthardt2011using] changes the control action (M04) and the sensor (M05); both are standard. Its Sec. 1 first claims are contradicted by its own Sec. 4, which lists earlier ECoG BCIs using word articulation [@leuthardt2004brain; @schalk2008two], and the broad speech-network wording by an uncited closed-loop speech-cortex BCI [@guenther2009]. The narrow claim, different overt vowels driving an ECoG cursor, holds for two patients; different imagined vowels were not tested. Results beat a 46.2% white-noise floor, but condition is confounded with patient and Table 2 disagrees with Fig. 8. Today attempted-speech BCIs reach 99.6% on 50 words on day one [@card2024].
